_comment_cooldown: Once someone gets an auto-reply, they won't get another for this many hours. Stops repeat replies during a back-and-forth.
_comment_agent: When enabled, a matching keyword starts a real conversation instead of sending one canned reply: the assistant asks what they need, collects the details, and emails you the same template the website form sends. Needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and EMAILJS_PRIVATE_KEY set on the host — without them it quietly falls back to the canned replies. Check /admin/status?token=... to see whether it is actually ready. Set enabled to false to go back to plain keyword replies.
_comment_startCooldown: Replaces cooldownHours while the agent is on, and is short on purpose. cooldownHours stops the same canned reply going out twice; a conversation is meant to be a back-and-forth, so the week-long gate would instead silence anyone whose conversation was lost to a restart. This is only the gate on STARTING a new conversation.

agent.businessContext: Deka shoots portraits, weddings, quinceañeras, concerts, events and brand content, and also does videography and graphic design. He is based in San Diego and works in both English and Spanish.

_comment_followUp: Appended to the rule's reply so the whole thing arrives as ONE message, then the signature after it. Same form for every rule; add "followUp": false to a rule to skip it there. Set to null to switch it off everywhere.

_comment_language: Each reply has an 'es' and an 'en' version. The whole message is scored to decide which to send, so a message that opens in one language but is mostly written in the other gets answered in the one it is mostly written in. defaultLanguage is used only when a message is too short or too mixed to call.
_comment_skipIfContains: If a message contains ANY of these, it is never auto-replied to — even if it also matches a rule keyword. Use for your regulars and casual talk.
_comment_rules: Checked top to bottom — the FIRST rule with a matching keyword wins, so put specific rules above general ones. Keywords are matched case- and accent-insensitively anywhere in the message.
